A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CLOC study. All pages, including equations, tables, figures and appendices, are readable and support comparison despite extensive reformatting and appendix renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original CLOC pre-training and downstream experiments, including image and region recognition, retrieval, Ferret and LLaVA evaluations, and appendix analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results in Tables 2–5 and the appendices, including ablations and the comparison of fine-tuning against training from scratch.

M1.justification: The CLOC losses, Prompter, grounding head and VESL stages remain unchanged. However, v2 Section 4 names VeCap2 instead of VeCap, while its dataset description, Figure 3 and Appendix C.1 still specify VeCap. The PDFs do not resolve whether this represents a component replacement or a naming/reference update.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the WiT/DFN training corpora and the same image-level, region-level, Ferret and LLaVA evaluation coverage. RefLVIS in v2 Table 4 denotes the existing referred-object classification task rather than an added dataset or scenario.

E2.justification: Tables 2–5 retain the same CLIP/OpenAI-CLIP baselines, Shikra, detector alternatives and model variants. OAI-CLIP abbreviates OpenAI-CLIP; newly discussed captioning approaches and the UMG-CLIP citation do not introduce additional evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: The stated training and evaluation settings remain unchanged, including Table A hyperparameters, the 2K-image GRIT validation sample, recall@10, GPT-4o evaluation of Ferret-Bench, and the frozen/unfrozen LLaVA configurations. No revised evaluation protocol or additional experimental setting is documented.

E4.justification: The Prompter, VESL, detector, text-filtering, grounding-loss, region-count and scaling ablations are retained. Figure A contains identical examples, and the fine-tuning-versus-training-from-scratch analysis moves from Appendix C to D without substantive changes.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. Both retain the same assertion that the sampled GRIT validation set is statistically stable.

E6.justification: The dataset statistics and numerical results in Tables 1–5 are identical. The appendix also retains the same COCO/LVIS recognition results: 64.1/19.1 for additional fine-tuning and 70.1/27.2 for the referenced model trained from scratch.

T1.justification: Equations 1–4 and their mathematical definitions are equivalent across versions. Introducing an intermediate p in Equation 2 and shortening BoxHead to Head are notation changes; no new assumptions, derivations, theorems or proofs appear.

C1.justification: Both versions claim promptable region embeddings, scalable region-text labeling and improved downstream use of CLIP through CLOC. The revised introductory question emphasizes zero-shot region recognition and retrieval already claimed and evaluated in v1, without changing the contribution scope.

C2.justification: Section 2 adds a substantive rationale for favoring contrastive pre-training over decoder-based captioning: smaller training batches and lack of direct language alignment are presented as scalability and retrieval disadvantages. The interpretations of CLOC results, limitations and future directions remain substantially unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 removes the AXLearn implementation disclosure and repository link, and the direct GRIT download link. Hyperparameters, labeling pseudocode, hardware/runtime information and pending-release statements remain; the reproducibility statement is relocated to Appendix A rather than newly added.

R1.justification: v2 expands related work with captioning-based pre-training, LocCa and MaskCLIP, adds the Lai et al. 2025 captioning reference, and removes the MM1.5 citation. These changes broaden contextual comparisons while retaining the original positioning around improving CLIP localization.

P1.justification: v2 condenses sentences and captions, shortens headings, reorders related-work topics and moves the reproducibility statement into the appendix, shifting the existing appendix letters. The main narrative and most explanatory passages remain closely aligned with v1.

P2.justification: The document switches throughout from single-column to two-column layout. Several tables become column-width displays, Table 5 replaces its repeated MLLM column with grouped blocks, and Listing 1 wraps across pages. All four figure assets are identical but resized or relocated.

improvement.justification: v2 adds useful context about captioning-based alternatives, but removes implementation/access information and introduces unresolved VeCap/VeCap2 naming. The experimental evidence and substantive limitations are unchanged. These contextual gains and documentation drawbacks leave the net quality direction uncertain.
